Because they're old. They have houses; probably two or three. So they want property prices to go up, higher market valuations making sense as they own most stocks. Youth care for the poor makes sense because they need good medical care. If poor people are standing in line, that's a problem for them. So kill the poor and they'll have better access to healthcare if that frees up the system. Mass immigration means cheap labor; old folks—70 or 80 years old—need gardeners, cooks, nurses.

Right? Immigrants: do you want to be gardeners, cooks, laborers? You don't want to. So we need immigrants and everything else. Inflation, economic growth, lower birth rate, gaslighting; it doesn’t affect them. Does that make sense? Rich pensioners drive trends; they’re responsible for what's going on. How can we understand this?

In human history, never have so many old rich people existed before. People 75 and older were a small fraction in 1900 but grew fast over 60 years. The problem: if they keep living, accumulating resources increases inequality. Not all old are rich; stats show wealth is evenly distributed among demographics. But there are lots of old-rich people.

Old rich are the problem because they want their pensions. Pension systems assumed old people would die (retirement age was 65, expected death at 72). They’re not dying, creating pension plan liabilities going up. Assumption changes: first, OPs will die; they're not; second, stock market investments improve yearly; volatility means losses for pension funds.

Pension fund returns are volatile; young people shouldn't put money in. As you grow, the pension fund won’t have enough for retirement because too many retirees and not enough workers. In 2001, there were 7.6 retirees for every 12.7 workers.
